issues.description: The UML in the problem statement names the Ride attribute 'abbreviation: char' (and therefore students expect a corresponding getter, e.g. getAbbreviation()). The reference solution declares the same concept with a different identifier: the field is named 'shortName' and the getter is getShortName(). This divergent identifier for the same conceptual attribute (Ride's abbreviation/short name) creates an unnecessary mapping burden: students reading the UML/description will look for 'abbreviation' but find 'shortName' in the code, and automated tests or grading that expect the UML name may fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the identifier across artifacts. Rename the Ride field and its accessor in the solution (and template) from 'shortName' / getShortName() to 'abbreviation' / getAbbreviation(), and use 'abbreviation' as the constructor parameter name. This matches the UML ('-abbreviation: char') and removes the mapping confusion for students.
